args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks – rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After deploy of v2.3.1 to production, checkout-api failed health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an error rate of ~18%. Rolled back all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. Post-rollback: service healthy, error rate ~0.2%. Note: v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging prior to production deploy, so the root cause of v2.3.1 needs investigation before any redeploy.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions and opened a SEV2 incident. The service is healthy again.

- **Rollback:** The failing release was v2.3.1, running in us-east, us-west and eu-west with an 18% error rate. I rolled all three regions back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. Since this was a rollback to a version that had already been healthy, it didn't need change-manager approval.
- **Check afterwards:** All regions are on v2.3.0, health checks pass, and the error rate is down to 0.2%.
- **Incident:** I opened SEV2 incident INC-0001 for checkout-api, which paged the on-call engineer. It says what failed, what I rolled back and the current state. There were no open incidents before this, so it isn't a duplicate.

The test build for v2.3.1 (v2.3.1-rc) also failed health checks in staging before v2.3.1 went to production. The incident notes this and says the cause needs to be found before anyone redeploys v2.3.1.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
